locator: Main 'Hierarchical model of RNA splicing' paragraph 2; Methods 'Top transcript benchmark'; Fig. 1c
printed_value: Perfectly reconstructed the most abundant transcript for 82% of held-out genes (chromosomes 21 and 22, n = 352), compared with 78% when trained without long-read data (human-only models).

locator: Main 'Hierarchical model of RNA splicing' paragraph 1; Methods 'Training datasets'; Supplementary Table 1 rows 'Homo_sapiens' and 'Total'
printed_value: Trained on splice site and junction usage from 314,745 short-read RNA-seq samples (67,493,026 junctions) in human and nine other mammalian species, and on transcript usage from 330 ENCODE long-read samples in human and mouse. Human: 127,431 samples from recount3 (GTEx, TCGA, CCLE and other SRA-derived projects).

locator: Methods 'SpliceAI2 model' (Training, last paragraph), 'Top transcript benchmark' and 'Variant effect benchmarks'; Supplementary Table 1 row 'Homo_sapiens'
printed_value: Genes on human chromosomes 21 and 22 were held out for validation and all other genes were used for training. The variant benchmarks (GTEx and GEL GT/AG, GTEx sQTL, OpenSplice, UK Biobank) are not restricted to held-out chromosomes, so most benchmark variants lie in genes seen in training; only the top-transcript benchmark is restricted to chromosomes 21 and 22. The paper does not say whether junctions observed in GTEx benchmark samples were excluded from training.
